question: How is a private .cockpit/ kept per branch and synced between machines?
tldr: Saved per commit and branch in a private repo, pulled back on checkout.
answer: A cockpit-owned git store keeps refs per project, commit and branch; switching branches saves one description and restores the other, and a push to a private repo on the same forge syncs machines.
why: The ref layout and the switch rules decide which description you see; prose alone hides them.

nodes.label: .cockpit/ on disk
nodes.explain: Excluded from the project's git through .git/info/exclude.

nodes.label: Private store
nodes.explain: One bare repo per forge host, with refs c/<sha>, b/<branch> and kept/<n>.

nodes.label: Branch switch
nodes.tldr: Save the old, restore the new
nodes.explain: Uses the branch's own description, else the nearest earlier commit's, else what you had.

nodes.label: cockpit-private repo
nodes.tldr: Your own repo on the same forge
nodes.explain: Pushed and pulled so another machine's newer description comes in.
